title: STEP BY STEP THROUGH THE WILDERNESS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites moved on and camped at Oboth. Then they set out from Oboth and camped in Iye Abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab toward the sunrise. From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley. They set out from there and camped alongside the Arnon, which is in the wilderness extending into Amorite territory. The Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. - Num 21:10-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At first glance these verses seem like a simple travel log, a list of place names we can barely pronounce. Why does Scripture record them? Because God cares about the journey, not only the destination.

Each of these camps marked a real day in the lives of real people. Every stop meant setting up tents, gathering food, tending children, and then packing up to move again. The journey was slow and often unremarkable, yet the Lord was leading them every single step.

There is quiet comfort in this. God's faithfulness is not only for the dramatic moments of victory or the crisis of the snakes. He is just as present in the ordinary stretches, the long marches between one place and the next. He was writing down each stop because none of it was wasted.

Perhaps you feel you are in an unremarkable season, simply moving from one ordinary day to the next. Take heart. The God who recorded each Israelite campsite is walking with you through every plain, uneventful stretch of your life. In Christ, not one step of your journey is meaningless. He is leading you home (Heb 11:16).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust God's presence in the ordinary, unremarkable days?
2. How does knowing God records your journey change how you see it?
3. What "in-between" season are you in right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are with me in the ordinary stretches, not only the mountaintops. Lead me step by step, for I know You are guiding me home. Amen.
